channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [9] Topological Fermi arc interference on low-symmetry Weyl surfaces
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Quansheng Wu, Oscar Tjernberg

Authors: Cong Li, Zhilong Yang, Hongxiong Liu, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Highly relevant study on Weyl semimetal surface states and electronic spectra reconstructions.

Tags: #experiment #NdAlSi #Weyl-semimetal #Fermi-arcs

Abstract: Bulk-boundary correspondence in Weyl semimetals is difficult to interpret on low-symmetry facets. Here, the authors resolve this issue on the NdAlSi(103) surface, showing that phase-shifted bulk-zone projections hybridize Fermi arcs into reconstructed, replica-rich surface spectra.
